## Verifier: **pass** Built the app (`npm ci && npm run build`) and ran the production server (`npm run start -- --port 3000`) with the sandbox environment sourced from `.factory/sandbox/.runtime.env`, then worked through the four acceptance checks in Chromium and over HTTP. All four pass; evidence is in the report above. ### Acceptance checks | \# | Check | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | First heading reads exactly `Invoices (5)` | **pass** — `

Invoices (5)

`, screenshot and close-up | | 2 | 5 body rows, matching the heading | **pass** — INV-1001...INV-1005, counted in the DOM and visible in the screenshot | | 3 | Literal `Invoices (5)` in the served HTML, no `` markers | **pass** — `curl` finds the literal string; zero `` in the whole document | | 4 | Button still `Export 3 invoices as CSV`, still downloads 3 invoices | **pass** — clicked it; Chromium downloaded `invoices-2026-11-21.csv` with 3 data rows | ### What I did, per check **1 and 2.** Opened ` (localhost/redacted) The accessibility snapshot reads `heading "Invoices (5)" \[level=1\]` , then `button "Export 3 invoices as CSV"\`, then a table whose body rowgroup has five rows: INV-1001 Acme Bakery, INV-1002 Northwind Books, INV-1003 Globex Coffee, INV-1004 Initech Hardware, INV-1005 Hooli Cleaning. The number in the heading equals the number of rows rendered. **3.** ` curl -s (localhost/redacted) returns `<main><h1>Invoices (5)</h1><button ...` verbatim. `grep -F` finds the literal string; `grep -o '<\!-- -->' \| wc -l` over the whole document returns **0**. Reading `h1.innerHTML` back in the browser after a reload also gives the plain string `Invoices (5)\`, so the single-template-literal form holds server-side and after hydration. **4.** Clicked the button. The network panel shows `GET /invoices/export => 200` with `content-type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `content-disposition: attachment; filename="invoices.csv"`, `cache-control: no-store`, and Chromium downloaded `invoices-2026-11-21.csv`: a header row plus INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003. The draft INV-1004 and the void INV-1005 are absent, which is the product rule the runbook calls out. ### Ways this could have looked right and been wrong - **Hardcoded number.** It is not: the heading interpolates `invoices.length`, the same array `` maps over. `exportable.length` still feeds `ExportButton` on the line below, unchanged. - **Comment markers.** The failure mode the spec warns about does not occur — 0 markers server-side, and `h1.innerHTML` is clean after hydration. - **Second click.** Clicked export twice; the second click downloaded the file again and the button returned to `Export 3 invoices as CSV` rather than sticking on `Preparing...`. - **Reload.** Same heading, same 5 rows, same button label. - **A different route in.** Navigated from `/` via the `Go to invoices` link (client-side nav, no full page load): `Invoices (5)`, 5 rows, no comment markers in the `h1`, 0 console errors. The only console error in the whole session was a pre-existing `favicon.ico` 404 on direct load, unrelated to this change. ### Notes - `npm test` passes: 30 tests across 4 files, including the two new cases in `app/invoices/page.test.tsx`. I treat that as a separate gate — the verdict above rests on the running app. - **Empty / filtered case not exercised.** The invoice list is a hard-coded `readonly Invoice[]` in `lib/invoices.ts`, so there is no way to make the table render 0 rows without editing code. The claim that the heading would follow a filter added later rests on reading the source (`invoices.length`), not on running it. This is not one of the acceptance checks and does not affect the verdict, but it is worth knowing when the status filter in #27 lands. - Nothing in the repo was changed. The working tree is as I found it, and the server and browser were stopped. > Generated by [Verifier](https://github.com/bsf-fixtures/ts-webapp/actions/runs/44929205079) for #41 · claude · opus50 · \~98 AIC · ⌖ \~22 AIC · ⊞ 2.7K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Absf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp+%22gh-aw-workflow-call-id%3A+bsf-fixtures%2Fts-webapp%2Ffactory-role-verifier%22&type=issues)
